label: PF Backlog 565
title: Governance: every backlog item must belong to an epic (analyze-first; 'Unscoped' last resort; grooming re-homes)
body:
## Goal
Every backlog item belongs to an epic, going forward, across the board.

## Behaviour
- Add time: try to fit an existing epic (`backlog.suggest_epic`); if none fits -> the `Unscoped` holding epic.
- Human/agent: if no epic fits, ASK and create the epic first.
- Grooming: highlight `Unscoped` children + a suggested epic -> create a new epic or move them.

## Implementation
- `core/backlog.py`: `suggest_epic`, `auto_epic`, `ensure_unscoped_epic` (holding epic), `epic_coverage_warnings`,
  `unscoped_children`, `is_holding_epic`; add-time warning when an item has no epic.
- Automated creators (intake/issues/insights/ops/intake_channels) attach `auto_epic(...)`.
- `core/grooming.py`: `unscoped_review` + highlight at the review/approve step.
- Gate `scripts/dev/backlog_epic_audit.py` (baseline-aware; fatal for NEW unparented items) wired into precheck;
  advisory `epic-coverage` in `wired_audit`.
- Rule: AGENTS.md + docs/ADDING-TO-PRODUCT-FORGE.md (recipe A).

## Acceptance (G/W/T)
- Given a NEW open non-epic item with no epic, when the gate runs, then it FAILS.
- Given an automated create with no matching epic, then it lands under `Unscoped` (not unparented).
- Given grooming, then `Unscoped` children are listed with a suggested epic.

## Follow-up
BI-PF-1251 (Unscoped triage loop).
